questions.stem: A cooling-system brief asks why constant-pressure heating of a gas needs more heat than constant-volume heating to reach the same temperature.

options.text: Because the gas does more internal work on its own molecules while expanding
options.misconception: invents internal work during expansion

options.text: Because the expanding gas does boundary work on the surroundings, so some heat goes to work
Because the constant-pressure gas is denser and therefore heats more slowly
options.misconception: blames gas density for the extra heat

options.text: Because at constant pressure the molecules collide with the wall more slowly
options.misconception: suggests slower wall collisions need more heat

questions.explanation: At constant pressure the gas expands and does work on the surroundings, so Q = ΔU + W exceeds the constant-volume value for the same rise. The extra heat is not stored internally.
questions.hint: Ask where the extra heat goes on the expanding path.

questions.stem: Calculate the work done by a gas that expands at a constant pressure of 200000 Pa while its volume grows from 0.0150 m3 to 0.0240 m3.

questions.topic: Molar heat capacity at constant volume
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant-volume heat capacity of an ideal diatomic gas
questions.stem: What is the molar heat capacity at constant volume of an ideal diatomic gas at ordinary temperatures, in joules per mole per kelvin?
questions.explanation: A diatomic molecule has three translational and two rotational modes, so Cv = (5/2)R = 20.785 J per mol K when vibration is frozen out. The monatomic value ignores the rotations.
questions.hint: Five active modes give five halves R.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Why no work is done at constant volume
questions.learningObjective: Explain why paddle stirring can heat a gas in a sealed insulated vessel
questions.stem: A brief asks why a gas in a sealed, rigid, insulated vessel can have its temperature raised by stirring with a paddle.

options.text: Because the paddle work cannot be done inside an insulated vessel without a temperature difference
options.misconception: claims paddle work needs a temperature difference

options.text: Because the vessel is insulated, so the paddle work escapes immediately through the walls
options.misconception: thinks insulated walls carry the paddle work away

options.text: Because the paddle stores kinetic energy that never converts into thermal energy
options.misconception: denies conversion of mechanical into thermal energy

options.text: Because a rigid vessel allows no boundary work, so paddle work raises the internal energy

questions.explanation: With a rigid boundary there is no boundary work, so paddle work increases the internal energy and hence the temperature even with no heat input. The distractors think insulation blocks that.
questions.hint: Ask whether the paddle work can leave as boundary work.
